title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
prompt:
Given two integer arrays `preorder` and `inorder` representing the preorder and inorder traversal of the same binary tree (with no duplicate values), reconstruct the binary tree and return it.

Since this is a coding exercise rather than an interactive class-based design, the function returns the rebuilt tree serialized to a level-order array (`null` for missing children, the standard LeetCode serialization) using the provided `tree_to_level_order` helper, so the result can be checked for equality.

examples.explanation: The first element of preorder (3) is the root; in inorder it splits [9] (left subtree) from [15,20,7] (right subtree).

constraints: preorder and inorder consist of unique values
Every value in inorder also appears in preorder
preorder is guaranteed to be the preorder traversal and inorder the inorder traversal of the same binary tree
hints: The first value in preorder is always the root of the (sub)tree currently being built.

Find that root's value in inorder — everything to its left in inorder belongs to the left subtree, everything to its right belongs to the right subtree, which tells you how many elements to take from preorder for each side.
Use a hash map from value to index in inorder for O(1) lookups, and recurse with a shared pointer/index into preorder that always points at the next unused root.

solution.approach: The first element of preorder is always the root. Look up that value's position in inorder using a precomputed value-to-index map; everything left of it in inorder is the left subtree, everything right is the right subtree, and their sizes tell us how many preorder elements belong to each side. Recursively build the left subtree first (consuming the next chunk of preorder via a shared index), then the right subtree. Finally serialize the rebuilt tree back to a level-order array.
